heading: INT. SALT MINE - SEALED CHAMBER, DEPTH 600 FEET - NIGHT SHIFT

units.text: INT. SALT MINE - SEALED CHAMBER, DEPTH 600 FEET - NIGHT SHIFT
A cathedral of white.
Walls of rock salt rise forty feet, glittering where the lamps touch them.
Iron rails vanish into a black tunnel to the east, now choked with rubble.
The air is dry as paper.
FOREMAN AUGUSTIN BRANDT, fifties, broad as a doorway, stands with his back to the rubble, his lamp swinging.

Around him, four miners have gathered: young PETRU VASILE, nineteen, still clutching a lunch tin; veteran HANNELORE KRUG, sixties, a woman with a face like a closed fist; JIN-HO PARK, thirties, the surveyor, unrolling a map; and the new hire, MBALI DLAMINI, twenties, who has not yet been told she is useful.
We are not in danger. We are in a pause.
units.name: AUGUSTIN

units.text: How long is a pause?
units.name: PETRU

units.text: Until they dig.
units.name: AUGUSTIN

units.text: The east shaft is gone. But the old ventilation line runs north.
units.name: JIN-HO

units.text: Old is the word.
units.name: HANNELORE

units.text: I'm only saying it exists.
units.name: JIN-HO

units.text: Mbali sets her pack down.
Takes out a thermos.
Sets it on a salt block.
Her hand does not shake, and the others notice it does not.
There's water for three days if we're careful.
units.name: MBALI

units.text: Three days is plenty.
units.name: AUGUSTIN

units.text: He smiles.
It does not reach his eyes.
Hannelore sees it.
Jin-ho sees her seeing.
Petru offers his lunch tin around.
Everyone declines.
He tucks it back in his jacket and pats it twice, as if it were a pet.
Behind them, a low crack.
A thin seam opens in the wall.
Salt dust drifts like snow.
All five heads turn.
All five stop breathing.
That's the rock settling.
units.name: AUGUSTIN

units.text: Rock does not settle at six hundred feet.
units.name: HANNELORE

units.text: It does if it's being told to.
units.name: JIN-HO

units.text: They scatter, five lamps flinching in five directions, then regroup at the far wall.
Mbali is the first to speak.
Foreman. How many were in the east tunnel when it came down?
units.name: MBALI

units.text: Augustin looks at her.
The seam widens, a soft hiss of wind from somewhere that should not have wind.
Eight.
units.name: AUGUSTIN

units.text: Silence.
But we counted five.
units.name: PETRU

units.text: Yes.
units.name: AUGUSTIN

units.text: Hannelore takes a slow step back.
Mbali's lamp catches the seam.
Behind it, something pale shifts, and a hand, human, reaches out and curls around the salt.
